description: Essential first aid procedures, emergency response protocols, and life-saving techniques

primary_survey.acronym: DR ABC (Danger, Response, Airway, Breathing, Circulation)
primary_survey.danger: Ensure scene is safe before approaching
primary_survey.response: Check for consciousness (tap shoulders, call out)
primary_survey.breathing: Look, listen, feel for breathing (10 seconds)
primary_survey.circulation: Check for pulse; start CPR if absent

adult.breaths: 2 rescue breaths (tilt head, pinch nose, seal lips)
adult.hand_position: Heel of hand on center of chest, between nipples

cpr.child_1_to_puberty: Same ratio; gentler compressions; 2 fingers for infants
cpr.hands_only: 30 compressions/min without breaths; acceptable if not trained in rescue breathing
cpr.aed: Use as soon as available; follow voice prompts
cpr.continue: Until emergency services arrive or person recovers

adult_conscious.recognize: Cannot speak, cough, or breathe; hands at throat
adult_conscious.5_back_blows: Firm blows between shoulder blades with heel of hand
adult_conscious.heimlich: Abdominal thrusts; fist above navel, below sternum; sharp upward thrusts
adult_conscious.alternate: 5 back blows then 5 abdominal thrusts until cleared

choking.infant: 5 back blows + 5 chest thrusts; never abdominal thrusts

bleeding_control.direct_pressure: Firm, continuous pressure with clean cloth
bleeding_control.tourniquet: Life-threatening limb bleeding; apply 5–7 cm above wound; note time
bleeding_control.wound_packing: For deep wounds; pack with gauze, apply pressure
bleeding_control.elevation: Raise injured limb above heart level

burns.first_degree: Redness only; cool with running water 10–20 min; no ice
burns.second_degree: Blisters; same cooling; cover loosely; seek medical care
burns.third_degree: Full thickness; call emergency; don't remove clothing
burns.chemical: Brush off dry chemicals; flush with water 20+ min
burns.electrical: Call emergency; don't touch victim if still connected

shock.treatment: Lay flat; elevate legs (unless head/spine/chest injury); keep warm; seek emergency care

anaphylaxis.treatment: Epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen) in outer thigh; call 911; repeat in 5–15 min if needed
anaphylaxis.position: Sit up if breathing difficulties; lay flat with legs raised if fainting

fractures.treatment: Immobilize in position found; apply splint; seek care
fractures.open_fracture: Cover with clean dressing; don't push bone back; seek emergency care

recovery_position.position: On side; top knee bent forward; head tilted back to maintain airway
